free_tier.stated: 300 GB after a mobile-client login; 100 GB on registration alone: '用户注册即有100G云空间，在手机客户端登录则升级为300G'

per_object_cap.stated: 1 GB per file on the web uploader, 4 GB on the desktop client, 10 GB on VIP and 20 GB on SVIP

retention.stated: Trash holds deleted files for 10 days. The free allowance was cut from 2 TB to 100 GB in 2020 for accounts not logged in for two years

egress.terms: Metered by throttle rather than by byte: non-member downloads are capped around 0.1 MB/s and anything sizeable needs the desktop or mobile client

tooling: an official open platform with OAuth 2.0 at pan.baidu.com/union/doc, for example GET /api/quota with an access token returning total, free and used in bytes; the OpenList BaiduNetdisk driver; a Baidu developer app is required
chaining: 300 GB per Baidu account and Baidu accounts need a phone number. At 0.1 MB/s the non-member throttle makes even 500 GB a day impossible, so the read path fails independently of the quota

limits.value: about 0.1 MB/s on a non-member download
1 GB per file on web, 4 GB on the desktop client, free
the free allowance drops to 100 GB for accounts idle for two years

identity_cost.detail: a Chinese mobile number. The open platform adds a developer app on top

reliability_note: Content scanning applies even to private files: matching files become unreadable for the uploader too. The free tier is effectively read-only at serving scale. The guest share path gets further than expected and then stops: /share/verify returns errno 0 with a randsk cookie and the page renders the real file tree, but /share/list answers errno 2 and every byte path needs BDUSS

binding_note: 300 GB is 60% of the filter and 0.1 MB/s is 8.6 GB a day, so the throttle binds first: the corpus would need 116 days of continuous reading to serve one day's target.
notes: One record for the provider and its two seed sub-findings, the 2 TB to 100 GB cut and the anonymous share path. The anonymous path is the more interesting of the two: it proves the share metadata is public and the bytes are not, which is the pattern the whole topic is built on.
